verses.text: So what advantage does the Jew have? What good is circumcision?
A lot, in every way. First of all, they were entrusted with God's words.
What if some of them were unfaithful? Does that make God unfaithful too?
Absolutely not! Let God be true, even if every person is a liar. As Scripture says, ‘So you will be shown right in what you say and win when you are judged.’
But if our wrongdoing makes God's righteousness stand out, what should we say? Is God wrong to bring judgment? (I'm speaking from a human point of view.)
Absolutely not! Otherwise, how could God judge the world?
If my lie makes God's truth shine even brighter and brings him glory, why am I still judged as a sinner?
Why not say—as some falsely accuse us of saying—‘Let's do evil so good can come’? Those who say that deserve their condemnation.
So are we better off? Not at all. We've already charged that both Jews and Greeks are under sin.
As Scripture says: ‘No one is righteous—not even one.
No one understands; no one seeks God.
Everyone has turned away; together they have become useless. No one does good—not even one.’
‘Their throat is an open grave; their tongues tell lies.’ ‘Viper venom is under their lips.’
‘Their mouths are full of curses and bitter words.’
‘Their feet rush to spill blood.
Ruin and misery mark their paths.
They haven't known the way of peace.’
‘There is no fear of God before their eyes.’
We know that everything the law says is spoken to those under the law, so every mouth will be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God.
No one will be made right with God by doing what the law requires. The law shows us what sin is.
But now, apart from the law, God's righteousness has been revealed. The Law and the Prophets bear witness to it.
This righteousness from God comes through faith in Jesus Christ to everyone who believes. There is no difference,
because everyone has sinned and falls short of God's glory.
Yet God freely makes people right through his grace, by the rescue that is in Christ Jesus.
God presented Christ as the sacrifice that deals with sin through faith in his blood. This showed God's righteousness, because in his patience he had passed over sins committed earlier.
He did this to show his righteousness now, so he could be just and also make right the person who trusts in Jesus.
So where is there room to brag? It's shut out. By what principle—works? No, by the principle of faith.
We conclude that a person is made right through faith, apart from doing what the law commands.
Or is God only the God of Jews? Isn't he also the God of Gentiles? Yes, he is,
since there is one God, who makes the circumcised right by faith and the uncircumcised right through faith.
So does faith cancel the law? Absolutely not! It confirms the law.
